$800K in Halton. Your real mortgage?

Example only: $800,000 resale home, first-time buyer, minimum down payment, insured mortgage, 25-year amortization.
1) Purchase price: $800,000.
2) Minimum down payment: 5% of the first $500,000 ($25,000) + 10% of the $300,000 above it ($30,000) = $55,000. Mortgage before insurance: $800,000 − $55,000 = $745,000 (93.1% of the price).
3) Mortgage insurance premium: at 90.01% to 95% loan-to-value the premium is 4.00% of the loan, so $745,000 × 4.00% = $29,800, added to the mortgage. A 30-year amortization (open to first-time buyers and new-build buyers) adds 0.20%.
Total mortgage: $745,000 + $29,800 = $774,800.

Not included: Ontario sales tax on the premium, which is paid at closing and can't be added to the mortgage, plus land transfer tax, legal fees and adjustments. Lenders also apply the stress test and their own qualifying rules.

Sources: CMHC, "Mortgage loan insurance cost" (premium table), and Sagen premium rates chart; Financial Consumer Agency of Canada, down payment rules; Department of Finance, Sept 16, 2024 (insured price cap $1.5M, 30-year amortizations). Checked Oct 29, 2026. Example only; eligibility and lender rules apply. Not mortgage, tax or legal advice.

Pre-approved in Milton? Not approved yet.

1) Myth: pre-approved means approved. A pre-approval is an estimate of what a lender may lend you. 2) The lender still reviews the home itself and may order an appraisal. 3) A new car loan or a job change before closing can change your approval. 4) Ask your lender how long your rate hold lasts, and what could end it.

Oakville, $900K, first home. Cash at closing?

Example only: $900,000 resale home, first-time buyer, insured mortgage.
1) Minimum down payment: 5% of the first $500,000 ($25,000) + 10% of the portion above it ($400,000 × 10% = $40,000) = $65,000.
2) Ontario land transfer tax: $900,000 × 2% − $3,525 = $14,475.
3) First-time buyer refund: up to $4,000 if you qualify, so $14,475 − $4,000 = $10,475.
4) Legal fees and title insurance: about $2,500 (an estimate; fees vary).
Total: $65,000 + $10,475 + $2,500 = $77,975.

Not included: sales tax on the mortgage insurance premium, adjustments (like property tax and utilities) and moving costs. Lenders also apply their own qualifying rules, including the stress test.

Sources: Ontario.ca, Land transfer tax (rates and first-time homebuyer refund, which requires you to be 18+, never to have owned a home anywhere, and to move in within nine months); Government of Canada (Financial Consumer Agency of Canada), minimum down payment. Checked Oct 28, 2026. Estimates only; eligibility and lender rules apply. Not mortgage, tax or legal advice.

Rates just rose. What about your monthly mortgage?

The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate 0.25% to 2.5% today, its first hike since 2023, and says another increase could be needed.
- Why: to keep high energy prices from spreading into broader inflation, now expected near 3.5% by year-end.
- Variable rate: your monthly mortgage could rise about $13 per $100K owed if your lender's prime rises the full 0.25% (example 3.43% to 3.68%, 25-year amortization; about $66 more a month on a $500K mortgage). With a fixed-payment variable, more of each monthly mortgage payment may go to interest instead.
- Fixed rate: no change until renewal; fixed rates follow bond yields.
- Buying: higher rates can lower what you qualify for under the stress test. Ask your lender about a rate hold.
- Renewing soon: compare your options early. Next decision: Dec 9.

Source: Bank of Canada, Oct 28, 2026; Reuters via BNN Bloomberg, Oct 28, 2026; example rate: Ratehub, Oct 28, 2026.
